title: Staying safe and responding to geomorphic hazards
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:45Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank point, Reducing a geomorphological hazard's impact, covers building rules, warnings and evacuation, but it does not teach personal drills such as drop, cover and hold on, or recovery help, so the new point teaches a broader idea.

draft.title: Staying safe and responding to hazards
card: People can lower their risk from a geomorphic hazard by getting ready. They learn the warning signs, follow official warnings and practise drills.
In an earthquake the advice is drop, cover and hold on. Drop to the ground, take cover under a sturdy table, and hold on until the shaking stops.
Communities plan ahead too. They set building rules so buildings can cope with shaking, and they run warning systems, such as tsunami alerts sent to phones and sirens.
After a hazard, communities help people recover. This can mean emergency shelter, clean-up crews and money to rebuild homes and roads.
draft.remember: People stay safe by following warnings and drills. Communities plan with building rules, warning systems and recovery help.

a.q: Which action is part of the drop, cover and hold on drill?
opts: Taking cover under a sturdy table
Running outside as fast as possible
Standing in a doorway and waiting
Moving to the tallest part of the building
a.why: The drill tells people to take cover under a sturdy table and hold on until the shaking stops. Running outside is tempting, but people can be hurt by falling objects while moving during shaking.
a.clue: The drill protects you from falling objects while you stay put.

b.q: A coastal town in Japan sends a tsunami alert to every phone after an undersea earthquake. Which type of community response is this?
b.why: An alert sent to people's phones before a wave arrives is a warning system. A drill is practice by people, not an alert, so it is tempting but wrong here. Recovery help comes after the hazard, not before it.
b.clue: Think about when the alert is sent, and who sends it.

a.best: Taking cover under a sturdy table
